fix(iab): keep vendor lists out of server-rendered page state (#1126)

## Overview

IAB server state currently puts the entire Global Vendor List into the
page. Keep the banner summary and a versioned reference inline, then
fetch the full list when the browser mounts the CMP. Public-list banners
retain their summary through SSR and hydration. Client-only vendor
allowlists wait for accurate filtered data.

Built on #1120, now merged into `v3`. Fixes #1122.

## Implementation

- Share the compact state contract across TanStack Start, Next.js,
Nuxt/Vue, SvelteKit/Svelte and Astro, with React and headless consumers
using the same summary and loader.
- Reuse manifest init routes to serve public lists with a one-day cache.
Reject a mismatched vendor-list version. Hosted init references read
only the list from the response, retain private caching, and replay
resolved country, region, language and GPC inputs.
- Queue early accept/reject/save actions until the list arrives.
Preserve explicit GVL options, custom vendors and vendor allowlists.
Cancel queued actions when visitor, policy or list context changes, and
let newer draft edits supersede queued blanket actions. Reload
references after initialization or language changes while retaining TCF
listeners; subsequent actions retry transient fetch failures.
- Serve Astro manifest references through its configured same-origin
init route. TanStack direct-backend mode uses the public manifest GVL
URL; an explicit `routePrefix` opts into a mounted local route.
- Keep custom fetch results in client manifest mode and Astro server
resolution. Retain inline data when authenticated server fetches cannot
be replayed by a browser reference.
- Mount the shared IAB runtime in Vue/Nuxt so consent saves encode TC
strings.
- Keep React, Vue and Svelte dialogs available after deferred-list
failures. Accept/Reject retry with a valid summary, while detailed Save
waits for the list. Preserve reopened dialogs during pending saves and
cancel Vue actions whose runtime handle changes. Publish one `tcloaded`
event per replacement without dropping retained TC data.

Two adjustments to the issue's proposal: loading starts on mount so CMP
initialization and stored-consent validation do not depend on a click;
cache headers omit `immutable` because translations can change
independently of the vendor-list version.

## Performance

Final production-page measurements on `df67127c9`, compared with #1120:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| IAB init JSON | 860,567 B | 6,616 B |
| TanStack IAB HTML | 952,346 B | 14,186 B |
| Nuxt hosted IAB HTML | 1,022,401 B | 27,631 B |
| TanStack cold TTFB, median | 18.4 ms | 4.3 ms |
| Nuxt cold TTFB, median | 31.3 ms | 14.2 ms |
| TanStack cold banner DOM present, median | 26.3 ms | 11.4 ms |
| Nuxt cold banner DOM present, median | 41.0 ms | 21.5 ms |
| TanStack cold CMP loaded, median | 77.2 ms | 56.0 ms |
| TanStack warm CMP loaded, median | 49.7 ms | 26.5 ms |

The production browser run uses a pinned GVL with 1,211 vendors and
seven cold/warm pairs after two warmup pairs. Complete banner text,
including the vendor count, is identical before and after. No layout
shifts or long tasks were recorded. The final shared runtime comparison
against merged #1120 passed all 81 budgets across 14 results. The final
bundle comparison passed all 30 budgets across 23 consumer fixtures.
Neither comparison had missing measurements.

These are localhost measurements without network or CPU throttling.
Banner DOM presence is not a paint metric. A cold browser still
downloads the full list separately, so network latency can delay a very
early action. Hosted context headers can require a CORS preflight.
TanStack's warm list request transfers zero bytes; hosted Nuxt init
remains private/no-store. The parent Nuxt build does not initialize the
CMP API, so it has no working readiness baseline. Nuxt's final cold/warm
CMP medians are 63.4/42.3 ms.

fix(core): serve stale manifests while revalidating (#1119)

Follow-up to the investigation in #1096. With Inth's `/manifest` behind
Vercel's CDN, the cold-instance cost that issue targets is one edge
round trip per instance. Two bigger problems sat next to it in the
shared in-process cache and affected every server adapter (Next,
TanStack Start, Nuxt, Astro, SvelteKit):

- **Revalidation stall every `s-maxage`.** `stale-while-revalidate` was
parsed but never served. When the fresh window lapsed, every in-flight
request blocked on the upstream ETag round trip even with a valid entry
in memory inside the advertised 24 hour stale window.
- **Outage turned warm pages into 10 s renders.** An expired entry plus
a hanging backend meant each request waited out the fetch timeout, then
Next and TanStack rendered without the banner.
- **Stale CDN responses were never cached.** When the CDN serves stale
during an origin problem, `Age` exceeds `s-maxage`, remaining lifetime
was zero, and the app refetched on every request.

## Change

`packages/core/src/libs/manifest-cache-runtime.ts`, plus one header on
two backend routes; no public API change, so all adapters pick it up.

- `CachedManifestResponse` gains `staleUntil` (`expiresAt` plus
`stale-while-revalidate`, minus upstream `Age`).
- Inside the stale window the cached entry is returned immediately and
one background revalidation runs with `If-None-Match`. Failures and
timeouts leave the stale entry in place.
- Background revalidation is throttled per entry to once per
`MANIFEST_DEDUPE_TTL_SECONDS`, keyed by a `WeakMap` on the entry object
so the record leaves with the entry and cannot outgrow the bounded
cache.
- Responses with `Age` inside the stale window are stored as already
stale instead of dropped.
- Eviction drops entries past `staleUntil` first, then LRU as before.
- A background fill never inherits the triggering request's `signal`; it
gets a cache-owned controller with the default timeout. The revalidation
floor counts from settlement. `s-maxage=0` keeps its stale window;
`no-store`, `no-cache`, and `private` disable it. A background 200 that
cannot be stored evicts the stale entry.
- A stale window is only granted when the response carries an explicit
`s-maxage`. `max-age` alone never opted into shared caching.
- The per-key revalidation floor is swept when lapsed, cleared when a
refresh lands fresh (so a backend with `s-maxage` under 5 s keeps its
own schedule), and kept only after a failed or already-stale refresh.
- New `onBackgroundRevalidate` option hands the background fill's
promise to the host, for runtimes that cancel detached work after the
response (Next.js `after`, Vercel `waitUntil`). Exposed on every server
adapter: `createNextConsentRouteHandlers`, TanStack Start's
`createConsentServerRoute` and `prefetchInitialConsent`, Astro's
`createConsentRouteHandlers`, SvelteKit's route handlers via
`ConsentManifestOptions`, and the Nuxt route factories. Where the
platform exposes a per-request lifetime handle the adapters use it by
default with nothing to configure: Nitro's `event.waitUntil` (Nuxt),
`event.platform.context.waitUntil` (SvelteKit on Cloudflare or Vercel
edge), and `locals.runtime.ctx.waitUntil` (Astro on Cloudflare). Next
and TanStack Start take the option explicitly since their platforms
expose `after` and `waitUntil` as imports rather than request fields.
Each path has a test.
- **Backend:** `/manifest` and `/c15t.js` now send the cache policy as
`CDN-Cache-Control` too. Vercel's CDN consumes `s-maxage` and
`stale-while-revalidate` from a bare `Cache-Control` and forwards
`public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, which I confirmed against a live
`*.inth.app` host. Without the second header an adapter reading through
the CDN never saw a shared-cache TTL and none of the above engaged. Inth
needs to deploy this backend change for the benefit to reach production.

## Verification

28 new regression tests in the core cache suites, plus one hook test per
adapter; full `@c15t/core` suite passes with coverage thresholds.
Adapter manifest tests pass for nextjs, tanstack-start, vue, astro,
svelte.

New harness `benchmarks/manifest-cache-bench` simulates a Vercel CDN
(edge and origin RTT, `Age`, 304s, stale serving, fault toggles).
Before/after from `RESULTS.md`, 25 ms edge, 150 ms origin,
`s-maxage=300`:

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold instance, 200 concurrent | 1 edge call, ~199 ms | unchanged |
| 20 rps over 900 s, 3 expiries | 200 stalled requests, 10 edge calls |
20 stalled (cold fill only), 5 edge calls |
| CDN serving stale, fresh app cache, 50 requests | 50 edge calls, every
request 26 ms | 4 edge calls, p95 < 0.1 ms |
| Origin down, warm app, 20 concurrent | each 26 ms | all < 0.1 ms |
| Edge unreachable, warm app | 5 rejections at 10 s each, no manifest |
served from memory < 0.2 ms |
| Edge unreachable, cold app | 3 rejections at 10 s | unchanged |
| Origin sends only `Cache-Control` through the CDN, 20 rps for 60 s |
n/a | 1120 of 1200 requests wait on an edge round trip |

Real production builds of the Next, TanStack Start and Nuxt bench apps
against a 150 ms fake upstream agree: sustained-load p95 dropped from
~190 ms to 29 to 52 ms, and a hanging backend went from a 10 s
bannerless TTFB to single-digit ms with the banner in the HTML.

Eviction under key minting was checked separately: with a visitor
minting a new `?language=` key per request, a manifest read at least
once per 128 junk requests stays cached; less often than that is evicted
and refetched, same LRU outcome as before.

## CI notes

The `performance / Runtime regression budgets` gate has failed on 4 of
11 completed runs on this branch, each time on `setConsent` or `saveAll`
with a different fixture size, and twice on pushes whose only diff was
one MDX file. Both budgets are defined as "at most 1 to 3 µs and 100%"
against sub-microsecond, timer-quantized base medians, so a single clock
tick trips them. The kernel paths they measure do not touch the manifest
cache. Reruns pass. A wider budget or more iterations is a separate fix.

## Not in this PR

- A shorter render-blocking timeout for the
cold-instance-with-unreachable-edge case (the only path that still
waits). Investigated; proposal is a `timeoutMs` on the core cache
surfaced as `manifestTimeoutMs` on adapter prefetch options, 2 to 3 s
for SSR prefetch, 10 s for route handlers. Separate PR.
- The build-time manifest seed from #1096. After this change it reduces
to pre-inserting a stale entry; deferred pending a decision on whether
one edge round trip per instance justifies a build step.

### Major Changes

- 4460e3e: This v3 alpha is for internal use only. APIs are unstable,
and breaking changes will occur between alpha releases.

Introduce the c15t umbrella package, shared consent runtime and policy
rules, rewritten backend, and new framework and script-tag integrations.
Update the CLI, IAB support, DevTools, and shared styles for v3.

Packages now ship ESM only. Keep related packages on compatible v3 alpha
versions.

Export `defineTheme` and the `Theme` type from the React, Next.js,
TanStack Start, and Vue entries so themes can use the same imports as
their framework integration.

Restrict iframe-blocker URL activation to HTTP and HTTPS. Replace
backtracking URL and theme parsing expressions, correct the PostHog
hostname boundary, and fix CLI layout detection for nested route groups
and locale directories.

Serve a stale consent manifest from the server adapters' in-process
cache inside the backend's `stale-while-revalidate` window while one
background request revalidates it, instead of blocking every request
after `s-maxage` expires; a failed or timed-out revalidation keeps the
stale manifest. The backend sends its manifest cache policy as
`CDN-Cache-Control` too, so Vercel's CDN forwards it. Add
`onBackgroundRevalidate` to the core cache and every server adapter for
runtimes that stop detached work after the response.

### Patch Changes

fix: remove consent UI loading delays in React and Astro (#1141)

## Overview

Cold consent UI can wait roughly 300 ms after its chunks finish loading
because React throttles Suspense retries. This affects the default
aggregate dialog, conditionally mounted compound exports, the widget,
and Astro's React IAB island.

Share a cached module subscription across React aggregate exports and
retry synchronously when each lazy export resolves. Keep the lazy
element and Suspense boundary stable to preserve server rendering and
hydration. The Astro client-only IAB island resolves its import through
component state.

The external-runtime provider now imports its small IAB context bridge
eagerly. Previously, children mounted in the fallback and remounted
about 302 ms later, which could erase draft input. The bridge does not
import the TCF runtime.

Vue/Nuxt did not reproduce the React retry delay. The separate
hover/focus preloading experiment was removed because it did not
demonstrate a cold-open improvement. Vue/Nuxt behavior is unchanged by
this PR.

Fixes #1140

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Performance

## Measurements

Median milliseconds from the real banner's Customize click to DOM mount,
without prior hover/focus. Fresh Chromium contexts, local development
servers, no CPU/network throttle. Ten samples for the default dialog;
five for each additional case.

| Case | Before | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| React default dialog | 307 | 29 |
| React compound dialog | 305 | 14 |
| React widget | 307 | 21 |
| Astro React IAB island | 364 | 91 |

The removed Nuxt experiment measured cold mount time of 26 → 45 ms. Five
development samples do not distinguish variability from a regression.
Its 7 ms result required a separate 200 ms hover condition and did not
address the immediate-click case. Historical measurements remain in the
report, clearly labelled as an experiment absent from the final code.

The external-runtime probe no longer remounts after loading. The final
default dialog reaches first visible / fully visible in 46 / 188 ms,
compared with 334 / 475 ms before. SSR hydration keeps the original DOM
node and working event handlers.

The Astro measurement exercises the actual island source under Next's
React renderer with a local initialized IAB runtime/GVL. It is not a
full Astro navigation or bootstrap benchmark. The user's original 568 ms
mount was not reproduced exactly; the fixture confirms the scheduling
delay. Production performance was not measured.

[Expanded report, raw samples and reproduction
commands](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/blob/t3code/fix-slow-dialog-first-open/benchmarks/reports/consent-loader-audit-2026-09-15/README.md).
[Initial default-dialog
investigation](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/blob/t3code/fix-slow-dialog-first-open/benchmarks/reports/react-dialog-first-open-2026-09-15/README.md).

Source inspection found no equivalent React retry pattern in Svelte, the
private Solid wrapper, or script/iframe/network-blocker loaders. Those
paths were not separately benchmarked.

## Validation

- 675 React tests and 240 Astro tests pass, with coverage thresholds
enabled. React coverage is 69.53% functions and 65.91% branches.
- 75 shared benchmark tests and eight repository docs tests pass.
- Regression checks fail with the old Astro loader, dropped external IAB
actions, and a missing preloaded-module retry notification. All pass
with the fix.
- React, Astro, Next.js and TanStack Start builds/type checks pass,
along with benchmark TypeScript and changed-file lint/format checks.
- The Astro browser test uses the same React source modules as the
suite. This fixes the previous CI coverage failure caused by counting an
additional compiled copy of React code. No coverage thresholds were
lowered.
- An existing persistence test now waits for the scheduled storage write
before asserting the saved record.
- Both benchmark CLIs reject invalid iteration counts, normalize local
filesystem resource URLs, and record source revision/dirty state. The
dialog summary includes download completion and download-to-mount
timing. Historical artifacts identify metadata that was not captured as
unknown.
- Release-plan validation includes `@c15t/react`, `@c15t/astro`,
`@c15t/nextjs`, `@c15t/tanstack-start`, and `c15t` at `3.0.0-alpha.2`.

The external IAB provider now also queues actions until its owner's
runtime publishes a handle, including propagating save failures. Queued
saves reject with AbortError on bridge teardown or replacement, while
StrictMode effect replay preserves pending actions. The owner must
unmount a borrowing provider when disposing its runtime. React and
Next.js v3 peer ranges require React/React DOM 18+, matching their
existing use of `useId` and `useSyncExternalStore`. The upgrade guide
documents this correction to the earlier alpha ranges.

Failed chunk imports remain cached until reload, matching the previous
React.lazy behavior. Retry UX is outside this fix. The linked issue now
includes the additional confirmed React/Astro cases from the follow-up
audit.

The previous reviewed revision edc8e48f5 passed GitHub CI:
repository/docs, package builds, package behavior/types, all supported
databases, all five browser integration groups, bundle budgets and
runtime budgets pass. The previous React coverage failure is fixed
without lowering thresholds. Full Local CI was unavailable because its
workflow-security job stopped with zizmor reporting "no inputs
collected"; the full validation completed on GitHub.

feat(core): vendor-level consent outside IAB (#1155)

## Overview

Adds vendor-level consent outside IAB TCF (#1034). A visitor can grant a
category and still turn one vendor off. A script, network rule or iframe
that names a `vendor` slug loads when its category condition passes
**and** the visitor has not turned that vendor off. Under an `iab`
policy the slug is inert and the TC string decides.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Preview (React preference center, from #1160) |
|:---:|
|
![Preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef51b3e2-4f21-4f36-8722-a53a02782f2d)
|

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

This is the first of three stacked PRs: schema + core + scripts here,
backend persistence next, then the React preference UI.

### Design

- **Gate.** `evaluateConsent` gains a `vendor` conjunct after the
category check, so an unknown category still throws. The same rule
applies to the script loader, the network blocker
(`NetworkBlockerRule.vendor`) and the iframe blocker (`data-vendor`).
The iframe blocker marks the frames whose source it moved, so removing
the last gate attribute from one restores its source while an author's
own lazy `data-src` is never promoted.
- **Storage.** Only denied vendor ids are stored, in a new
`<storageKey>-vendors` sibling record with a compact cookie projection.
Once a denial has existed, lifting the last one leaves a timestamped
empty record so a newest-wins merge with an older server read cannot
re-deny it. The consent envelope is untouched, so older bundles keep
reading the category choice. The record is read on the server from the
request cookie header too. It also carries the subject id, so a visitor
whose first act only decided vendors keeps one subject after a reload
even though no category record exists yet; that write only follows a
resolved subject when a vendor decision exists, so a category-only save
never clears a stored denial it did not hydrate.
- **Sources.** Vendors come from the runtime's `vendors` option, the
backend manifest (`vendors`, `vendorListVersion`, returned from `/init`,
as an empty list when the manifest declares none so a reinit can drop
them) and slugs on scripts, rules and `data-vendor` iframes, which the
iframe blocker declares the way the script loader and network blocker
do. Existence is the union; presentation from code wins over the
backend, and a code entry remembers the backend copy it replaced so
removing the code entry later brings the backend copy back. Backend
vendors a server prefetch already resolved are kept and merged, and a
later init replaces the previous backend list so an edit or removal
lands. A backend vendor that scripts also name falls back to a
script-sourced entry when the backend drops it, so the scripts stay
gated. A slug with no declaration still gates and warns outside
production; a slug that is not a valid wire id is dropped with a
warning, and a stored or hydrated denial outside that shape rejects the
record, so a tampered cookie cannot poison later saves. The script
loader and network blocker declare their owned slugs on construction and
on every list swap, so one introduced through `updateScripts` or
`updateRules` becomes toggleable and one whose script moved category
follows it. Owner conditions are copied before they reach the snapshot,
so freezing it never freezes a caller's script or rule config.
- **Save.** `save({ ...categories, vendors })`, `save(input, { vendors
})`, or a staged `runtime.stageVendorConsent()` / `set.vendorDraft()`.
The inline `vendors` key is split off before the category validator sees
it; the context form wins when both are given. `stageVendorConsent` is
named apart from the IAB handle's `setVendorConsent`, which sets a TCF
vendor by numeric id and takes effect at once. A vendor-only change
records without renewing category receipts, emits `vendors:recorded`
instead of `choice:recorded`, and sends the full grant map as
`vendorChoice` next to an empty v3 `choice`, so the backend does not
read the body as a 2.x submission and restamp every category from the
preference map. Accept all and reject all clear the denial list and
ignore any explicit vendor grants; narrowed to the displayed categories,
they only lift a denial when the selected categories settle the vendor's
condition together, whatever the categories left alone hold. A save that
never decided vendors sends no grant map; an explicit grant over no
prior decision records a timestamped empty list. Undeclared or
`disabled` vendors cannot be toggled on save, and a stored denial only
counts at the gate while the vendor is declared and toggleable; a vendor
removed from every declaration follows its category again, since no
switch is left to grant it, and a full accept or reject all still clears
its retained denial so it does not return blocked. Declarations passed
to `kernel.set.vendors()` are copied before the snapshot freezes them. A
`data-vendor`-only frame holds against every stored denial only until
its slug is declared; a `disabled` declaration then lifts a stale
denial, as it does at every other gate. A denial for a vendor that is
not declared right now still travels in the grant map as `false`, so a
vendor that disappears for one session and returns is still denied, and
a decision travels even with nothing declared: the backend keeps an
earlier decision for any vendor a later map omits, so a bulk clear after
the backend dropped a vendor names the lifted denial as an explicit
grant rather than sending an empty map. When a server prefetch seeds the
records, the persistence module still reads the vendor record's two
projections and applies the newer localStorage copy before any gate
runs, so a cookie the browser dropped does not pin an older denial list.
- **Not folded into the choice fingerprint.** Adding a vendor does not
reopen consent; new vendors default to on inside a granted category.
`copyRevision` stays the re-consent lever.

### Accepted gaps, documented in the release note

- Turning a vendor off does not delete cookies that vendor already set.
`clearOnRevocation` covers that by category.
- A vendor denial has no expiry and no policy basis. A saved vendor
decision carries the grant map and its time, not the `vendorListVersion`
label, which is shown and surfaced to dev tools only.
- Declaring backend vendors changes the manifest revision.

### Also

- `Script.vendorId` docs corrected: it is IAB-only. Outside IAB mode a
script carrying any IAB field is denied, which is unchanged behavior.
- `@c15t/scripts` integrations set `vendor` to their manifest slug and
send every Consent Mode, RudderStack and Clarity channel as denied while
the vendor is off.
- Dev-tools captures the two new kernel events.
- New docs page: Integrations → Vendor-level consent.

### Bundle budgets

The gate, codec with its subject copy, the paused-iframe marker and the
save path add about 3.5 kB gzip to the kernel entry on every consumer
scenario, the review fixes included. Every consumer bundle delta budget
carries a named `VENDOR_CONSENT_GZIP_BYTES` allowance for that, to be
removed once the feature is on `v3`.

### Review threads left open on purpose

- The generated `AGENTS.md` and package docs were regenerated from
`docs/`, not hand-edited.
- Persisting `vendorChoice` in `@c15t/backend` and returning
`subjectVendorChoice` is the next PR in the stack, #1156; this PR only
adds the wire contract.
- The vendor draft, like the category draft, is hidden rather than
cleared while the policy fingerprint differs. Changing that belongs to
both drafts together and is out of scope here.
- Categories a manifest vendor contributed stay in the inferred set
after a re-init drops that vendor. Removing them needs replacement
semantics for the inferred set, the same as a removed script's category
today, and is out of scope here.

An iframe with only `data-vendor` holds against every stored denial,
declared or not, since it has no category to follow; and a mounted
script loader or network blocker puts its slugs back into the declared
set whenever another source sweeps them out. Both close the cold-start
window where a backend-declared vendor could load before its `/init`
arrived. Each module's declarations are remembered per module, and every
slug an update names is rebuilt from what all modules declare: a slug a
measurement script and a marketing rule share stays under both
categories whichever module updates, two modules owning it under the
same condition keep it when one moves, and a slug nothing names any more
loses its script entry. Disposing a module rebuilds the slugs it named
the same way, so a vendor no live module owns stops being toggleable at
once. The iframe blocker's declaration follows the live frames: a frame
that changes its slug or category, or leaves the page, takes its old
pair with it. `declareOwnedVendors` and `forgetOwnedVendors` are
exported for hosts that mount their own loaders. A bulk action narrowed
to some categories decides a vendor when the outcome of its condition
flips between the selected categories set to what the action makes them
and the opposite, so a vendor under `{ not: marketing }` is decided by
rejecting marketing. An explicit grant over an already-empty decision
takes the action time like any other reconfirmation. A bulk action that
covers the whole choice scope, which is what every stock accept or
reject all sends, clears the list outright rather than deciding vendor
by vendor; an empty choice scope, where the visitor decides nothing, is
never covered. The stored denial list is read from whichever projection
is newer, and from localStorage on a tie, so a cookie write the browser
dropped for size cannot hide a denial or a resolved subject localStorage
holds. Narrowing a queued replay to the categories a newer action did
not supersede keeps the vendor map while it is still the current one;
only a newer action that carried its own map drops it.

## Related issues

Refs #1034

`packages/scripts`, `packages/dev-tools`: all green. 69 new test blocks

feat(backend): store vendor-level consent (#1156)

## Overview

Second layer of the vendor-level consent stack (#1034), on top of #1155.
The backend now stores the per-vendor grant map a v3 client sends and
returns it on read.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Preview (React preference center, from #1160) |
|:---:|
|
![Preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef51b3e2-4f21-4f36-8722-a53a02782f2d)
|

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

- **Migration `4-vendor-choice`** adds a nullable `consent.vendorChoice`
JSON column. Idempotent, checked before adding, same pattern as
migration 3. Run the migrator before deploying a client that sends
vendors.
- **`POST /subjects`** accepts `vendorChoice` on the cookie-banner body.
The confirmation time must not be later than the server clock. The map
is stored as sent, including ids the manifest does not declare: the
client merges backend and code-declared vendors, so the manifest is not
an allowlist for it.
- **`GET /subjects/:id`** returns each consent row's `vendorChoice` and
an aggregate as `subjectVendorChoice`: the most recent act by `givenAt`
decides every vendor it names, and a vendor an earlier act decided but
the latest one omits keeps that earlier grant, since a client on an
older vendor list never saw it. The aggregate's `confirmedAt` is the
time of the oldest decision still in it, so a retained grant is never
presented as newer than it is; an aggregate whose maps name no vendor at
all takes the latest act's time. The wire carries one time for the whole
map and the client merges whole records by it, so per-vendor timing
would need a wire change; dating by the oldest surviving decision is the
direction that never lets a retained older grant override a newer local
decision. A stored JSON `null` reads as absent on text columns too. Two
acts at the same instant are broken by row id compared by code unit, so
the answer depends neither on which row the engine returns last nor on
the host locale. A stored map that cannot be read conflicts with every
retry rather than passing as absent. A map that omits a vendor the
manifest declares is stored too: the client saw an older cached or
bundled manifest, a queued save replays the same map, and refusing it
would lose the whole act. The omitted vendor reads back as never decided
and follows its category, the same as a vendor added after the act.
- `/init` already returns `vendors` and `vendorListVersion` from the
manifest through the schema change in #1155.

### Replays against a row without a vendor map

A queued save can replay against a row an older backend wrote without
the vendor column, during a rolling upgrade or before migration 4. The
first version of this PR filled the map in on that replay, with a
racing-writer guard and a per-dialect JSON whitespace predicate to find
the row. That protected a rolling-deploy window multiplied by a lost
response, at the cost of the most complex code in the PR. It is gone:
the replay is accepted as the same act so the client's queue clears, the
row keeps no map, and the visitor's next save carries their full vendor
map, so the subject's aggregate catches up on their next act. A stored
map against a replay without one is still a conflict.

### Review threads left open on purpose

- A retry against a consent row stored under a legacy random id has no
map to compare, since those rows predate vendor maps.
- Per-vendor confirmation times in the aggregate would need a wire
change. The one time the wire carries is the oldest surviving decision,
which is the safe direction for a whole-record newest-wins merge.

with nothing to review and a record another island writes is not
overridden by a value the visitor never chose.

span gains a `consent-widget-vendor-name-*` test id: it is the switch's

by 6 pixel outline and closed vendor cards still visible. The Vue widget

feat: report manifest-mode sessions to the backend (#1169)

## Why

A host that resolves init from a cached manifest never calls `/init`, so
the backend cannot count the visitors it served. `/init` was the one
per-visitor request, and its request log was the visitor count. Manifest
mode removed it on purpose.

## What

Every server-side resolution now sends `POST /sessions` to the backend
after the fact, server-to-server and detached from the response. The
browser makes no request.

- **Wire contract** (`@c15t/schema`): `consentSessionReportSchema` and
`buildConsentSessionReport`. The body carries the manifest revision and
tenant, the matched policy (id, fingerprint, model, matched-by) or
`null`, resolution status, jurisdiction, country, region, resolved
language, GPC, a `source` of `render` / `route` / `init`, and the
adapter name. The visitor's user agent travels as `user-agent` and the
visitor's address on a dedicated `x-c15t-client-ip` header, derived from
the request's proxy chain and never taken from an incoming
`x-c15t-client-ip`; the backend applies its `ipAddress` masking and
tracking settings to it. Cookies are never forwarded.
- **Core** (`@c15t/core/server`,
`@c15t/core/transports/manifest-cache`): `reportConsentSession`. Fires
only for an absolute backend URL read as configured (a relative
`/api/c15t` is the app's own proxy; nothing is inferred from a manifest
URL, which may be a CDN), skips prefetch and prerender requests, times
out after 3 s, never throws or rejects even through a throwing lifetime
hook, and hands its promise to `waitUntil`. `createManifestTransport`
gains a `report` option for server callers.
- **Every resolution point reports**: Next.js init route and
`resolveConsent` (App and Pages Router), TanStack Start init route and
`resolveConsent`, SvelteKit init route, Nuxt init route, Astro init
route and middleware prefetch. Reports go through each adapter's
existing `onBackgroundRevalidate` hook (or the platform `waitUntil`
where one is detected), so a host already passing `after` or `waitUntil`
needs no change. Next.js `resolveConsent` gains `waitUntil` since it had
no hook. Every route reports after its vendor-list step, so a fallback
to hosted `/init` is not counted twice. `reportSessions: false` turns it
off everywhere.
- **Backend** (`@c15t/backend`): `POST /sessions` accepts only
server-to-server requests (a request carrying `Origin` or missing the
c15t protocol header is refused), rejects `source: 'init'` (reserved for
the backend), stamps the instance's tenant scope, writes the report to
the request's wide event, awaits a new `sessions.onReport` sink, and
stores nothing. The sink context carries an allowlisted header copy and
the masked `ip`; a host report names the visitor only on
`x-c15t-client-ip`, and `/init` reads the connection. The backend's own
`/init` emits the same event detached, skipping prefetches.
`defineConfig` rejects `sessions` like it rejects `observability`.

Browser-side resolution (static exports, `@c15t/browser`, Nuxt client
mode) does not report.

## Deduplication

None in the adapters. Every resolution emits one report; `source` and
the forwarded visitor headers are what a consumer dedupes and
sessionizes on. A page view can produce a `render` and a `route` report.

## Verification

- Type check, test-file type check, lint, and full test suites pass for
schema, core, backend, Next.js, TanStack Start, SvelteKit, Nuxt, and
Astro.
- New tests cover the helper, the manifest transport option, the backend
route and `/init` emission, the trust rules above, and one report case
per adapter. Existing tests that counted upstream fetches now filter out
the report or set `reportSessions: false`.

## Notes for review

- Reporting is on by default. Manifest-mode hosts start posting one
request per resolution to the backend after upgrade.
- In the Next.js App Router the render-path report runs without `after`
unless the host passes `waitUntil`; documented.
- Open bot threads on a page-view correlation key and opt-in IP
forwarding are design questions left for the maintainers.

Docs: self-host endpoints and configuration, deployment modes, upgrade
guide, Next.js optimization and data-fetching reference, and the
SvelteKit, Astro, TanStack Start and Nuxt quickstarts. Tegami note bumps
the eight packages minor.

The report carries the manifest revision, the matched policy, the jurisdiction, country, region, language and GPC signal. The visitor's user agent travels as `User-Agent` and the visitor's single client address on a dedicated `X-C15T-Client-IP` header, which the backend masks and records under its `ipAddress` settings; the forwarding chain itself is not sent, and neither are cookies. The browser makes no request. `@c15t/backend` adds the `POST /sessions` route and a `sessions.onReport` option. Reports are written to the request's wide event and handed to the sink; nothing is stored. The backend's own `/init` emits the same event, so one sink sees hosted and manifest traffic alike. fix(astro): restore stored consent on prerendered pages (#1178) Stack for Astro static builds: #1177 → #1178 → #1179 → #1180 → #1182 → #1183 → #1184 → #1185 → #1186 → #1187 → #1188 → #1189. On a prerendered page, a visitor's consent choice was lost on every reload. `readInitialConsentConfig` ran at build time even with `skipPrefetch`. It read the build request's empty cookie header and inlined `initialRecords: { choice: null }` and a build-time `now` into `__c15tAstroConfig`. The core runtime skips reading storage whenever the inlined config carries `initialRecords`, so the stored `c15t` cookie was never read back. ## Changes - `resolveConsentContext` takes a new `prerendered` option. It ignores the request headers and leaves `initialRecords`, `now` and `initialPrivacySignals` out of the inlined config, so the browser reads the visitor's own cookie. GPC is still detected in the browser. - The middleware passes `prerendered` and hands prerendered routes an empty `Headers`. That removes Astro's warning about reading `Astro.request.headers` on a prerendered page. - The client fills in `now` at boot when the inlined config has none. - `Astro.locals.c15t` gains a `prerendered` flag. #1179 uses it. This PR doesn't make the banner appear on static pages. That's #1179. ## Testing - New `prerender.test.ts`: a prerendered request whose `headers` getter throws, the inlined config with no visitor state, and hosted mode making no request at build time. - New `prerender.dom.test.ts`: a stored rejection is restored on a prerendered page, and a first-time visitor is asked. The restore test fails when the fix is turned off. - Package suite, `check-types` and lint pass. - In Chromium, against a bare Astro 7.3.2 static build with the full stack: after Reject All and a reload, the choice was restored and the banner stayed hidden. > [!NOTE] > ### Fix Astro consent middleware to restore stored consent on prerendered pages > - Prerendered pages previously inlined build-time visitor state, so returning visitors saw the banner again instead of their saved choice. Prerendered renders now resolve without reading request headers and strip initial records, privacy signals, and the clock from the inline config via `withoutVisitorState` in [server.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1178/files#diff-6e824be6756f6b144b8200318d22b2d64bb3e03de71492046ee8988d17146c4c) > - The browser client in [client.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1178/files#diff-b238632ea23e7bb76e0c5c68a45113edbde7c2bb16d2cdb65b7a96de0e83f387) supplies current browser time when the payload has no `now` value, so the prerendered client restores the visitor's stored cookie choice > - `waitUntilFromLocals` in [handlers.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1178/files#diff-14c38947c8f569bfe6f3e90935fe6af745e1eeebe825aa2c416233776a976520) now checks Cloudflare's Astro 6+ `locals.cfContext.waitUntil` before the Astro 5 `locals.runtime.ctx` fallback > - Expands the Astro peer dependency to major versions 5, 6, and 7 in [package.json](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1178/files#diff-31a85c0b4c5526a896f02b675a49f1f942ec15fa815f6326edc4f74248aa0048), and updates the quickstart docs for the Cloudflare context location difference > - CI parity selection in [ci-plan.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1178/files#diff-6ab94dd0fa95fc94c5b68cdab9bafc7c9c4b10337cb9df621eff2c41e4a47b2e) now selects React, Svelte, Vue, and Astro parity workspaces for an Astro Storybook change > - Behavioral Change: prerendered middleware skips hosted/manifest policy prefetch and defers policy resolution to the browser; `C15tLocals` gains a required `prerendered` property in [types.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1178/files#diff-117acc917c74b71c0565dcaa91170174ecb4b3bb8e7858070e022717823d3813) > > > > Macroscope summarized 74a3e97. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Fixed consent handling on prerendered Astro pages. Returning visitors’ saved choices are now read from their browser cookies, and first-time visitors can still see the consent banner. * Prerendered pages no longer depend on visitor-specific request data, avoiding Astro warnings about reading request headers during prerendering. * **Documentation** * Updated the Astro quickstart with details about consent behavior on prerendered pages.

fix(astro): show the consent banner on prerendered pages (#1179) Stack for Astro static builds: #1177 → #1178 → #1179 → #1180 → #1182 → #1183 → #1184 → #1185 → #1186 → #1187 → #1188 → #1189. `ConsentBanner` rendered nothing on a prerendered page. The build had no policy, so `hasConsentUi` was false even with `force`. In the browser, `syncBannerVisibility` could only show or hide a banner that was already in the HTML. ## Changes - **Offline mode:** the build now resolves the policy. In the browser, offline mode resolves without request geography, so the build gets the answer every visitor would. The banner renders with `hidden`, and the runtime shows it to visitors who have not chosen yet. The IAB banner gets the same hidden treatment. - **Hosted and manifest modes:** the policy depends on the visitor's location. `ConsentBanner` leaves an empty placeholder carrying its props and the stylesheet class names. Once the browser's init returns a policy that needs a banner, a lazily loaded renderer builds it there. - The banner's copy, actions, layout and class names now come from one shared model, `src/banner/prompt-model.ts`, used by both `prompt.astro` and the browser renderer. The "Secured by" tag shares a model with `branding.astro` too. - The renderer gets class names from the placeholder instead of importing the class maps. In the browser those imports pull in their CSS, and Astro links every stylesheet a page script can reach, so each page would carry a second copy of the banner CSS. - Returning visitors never download the renderer. - **Hidden banners now hide:** the banner CSS sets `display: flex`, which beats the `hidden` attribute. That meant a banner stayed on screen after a choice, on server-rendered pages too. A new `visibility.css` rule fixes it, imported from `@c15t/astro/styles.css`. - **Docs and CLI:** the quickstart's static pages section is rewritten, and the CLI boilerplate no longer tells users to avoid prerendering. ## Testing - A parity test renders `prompt.astro` and the browser renderer for an opt-in choice, an opt-out notice and a blocking wall, and compares the markup. - Tests for the hidden prerendered banner, the placeholder and its props, the runtime revealing the banner, and the placeholder being filled or left empty. - Package suite, `check-types` and lint pass. - In Chromium, with the full stack: - Offline, static: the banner shows on a first visit, hides after a choice, and stays hidden after a reload. - Hosted, static, against a mock backend that returns an opt-out notice: the browser drew the notice banner ("Do not sell or share my data" and OK), and dismissing it held across a reload. On the return visit the renderer chunk wasn't requested. - With the `[hidden]` rule removed, a hidden banner still computed `display: flex`. ## Not covered On a static page in hosted mode, the IAB banner still doesn't render. Only the standard banner has a browser renderer. > [!NOTE] > ### Fix hidden consent banner on prerendered Astro pages > - Prerendered pages now render the consent banner hidden when the policy is resolved offline, and the browser consent runtime decides when to show it > - Hosted and manifest pages with no resolved policy emit a hidden placeholder with serialized props; the browser client builds the banner from a shared prompt model and replaces the placeholder > - The browser client loads the prompt renderer as a lazy chunk, skips stale or duplicate renders, retries failed loads up to three times, and handles ClientRouter body swaps > - Moves translation, copy, class names, and branding resolution into shared models ([prompt-model.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1179/files#diff-b860905ab338ce039024567f80c7f2f83ecec428fa8526149c13300e3cddfcd7), [branding-model.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1179/files#diff-c470919df760d0701efb06e0564c2cad16f97305642fe52ab833e856b1aeabf0)) used by both server components and the browser renderer > - Risk: prerendered banners ship with `hidden` until browser synchronization; [visibility.css](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1179/files#diff-0b4b6f4fb6aebe221b4acd8d5647273d3eae34c1c7d63f372b301ab2612b3057) forces them to `display: none`, so pages without the JavaScript runtime keep the banner hidden > > > > Macroscope summarized 5234f9b. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Consent banners now work on prerendered Astro pages. Offline mode resolves policy at build time; hosted and manifest modes fill banner placeholders in the browser when needed. * Returning visitors’ stored choices are respected, while first-time visitors see the banner after the page loads. * Server-rendered pages can show consent banners on the initial render. Cached pages can use deferred, per-request banner rendering. * **Documentation** * Updated Astro guidance to explain rendering behavior across prerendered and on-demand pages, including when an adapter is needed. Prerendering is supported without requiring on-demand rendering.

fix(astro): add the component stylesheet to every page (#1180) Stack for Astro static builds: #1177 → #1178 → #1179 → #1180 → #1182 → #1183 → #1184 → #1185 → #1186 → #1187 → #1188 → #1189. The quickstart said the integration supplies styles, but it didn't. During the server build, the components resolve `@c15t/ui` class maps through the `node` export condition, which carries no CSS import. The banner shipped class names with no stylesheet. The dialogs were unstyled too: in an Astro 7 build their component CSS reached Vite's chunks but never made it into the output. ## Changes - The integration injects `@c15t/astro/styles.css` into every page with `injectScript('page-ssr', ...)`, plus the new `@c15t/astro/iab/styles.css` export when `iab` is set. - A new `styles: false` option turns this off, for sites that import the stylesheet themselves. - The demo and the CLI boilerplate no longer import the stylesheet by hand, which would now ship it twice. - The quickstart has a Styles section. ## Why the full stylesheet It costs about 16 KB gzipped, 125 KB raw. I tried a per-component bundle first: banner plus dialog came to about 11 KB gzipped. Two things made it unreliable: - The Svelte dialog uses primitive styles that only the full stylesheet contains. - Astro links every stylesheet a page's scripts can reach, including chunks that load later, so dialog CSS can't be deferred until the dialog opens anyway. feat(astro): show the prerendered banner at first paint when nothing is stored (#1185) Stack for Astro static builds: #1177 → #1178 → #1179 → #1180 → #1182 → #1183 → #1184 → #1185 → #1186 → #1187 → #1188 → #1189. A prerendered offline banner ships hidden, because the same HTML serves visitors who have already chosen. It stayed hidden until the page's module scripts loaded. An inline script right after the hidden banner, and after the IAB banner, now checks the cookie and `localStorage` for the consent keys: `c15t` (or the configured `storageKey`), its `-notice` sibling and the legacy `privacy-consent-storage`. If none exist, the visitor cannot have chosen, so it shows the banner and its overlay straight away. Anyone with a stored record still waits for the runtime, which validates it. The builder is exported as `buildBannerRevealScript` from `@c15t/astro/server`. A first-time visitor with GPC under a policy that owes them no banner would see it briefly, until the runtime hides it. The build has no GPC signal to decide that sooner. ## Testing - jsdom tests run the generated script against real cookies and `localStorage`: it shows the banner when nothing is stored, leaves it for a cookie, a notice dismissal or a legacy record, reads a custom `storageKey`, and targets the IAB banner's ids. - A prerendered banner includes the script, and a server-rendered one does not. - Package suite, `check-types` and lint pass. > [!NOTE] > ### Add first-paint inline reveal script for prerendered Astro banners > - Prerendered `ConsentBanner` and `IABConsentBanner` now emit an inline script right after the hidden banner that unhides the banner and overlay when no consent record is stored. It checks cookies and local storage, treats blocked storage access as no record, and leaves the banner hidden when any record exists so runtime validation still runs. > - Adds DOM tests for the generated script in [reveal-script.dom.test.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1185/files#diff-285999b694ce22ef23d3e9fd6347e2552d91808a83563232b5ed4c93325d684a) and extends the prerender suite in [prerender.test.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1185/files#diff-18092130f87c2ce6f2dd084b455991a7d1047a05f16ee4b854661791d9c31eec) to assert the script appears only for prerendered, hidden banners. > - Updates docs in [quickstart.mdx](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1185/files#diff-e022e451b304bbaeaa118cfaf207c82e15bfbb10016b1e227e4de22f483276d8) and adds a release note. > - Behavioral Change: visitors with a stored record see the banner only after runtime processing, same as before; only the empty-storage path reveals at first paint. fix(astro): stop dialog islands shipping a second copy of the stylesheet (#1188) Stack for Astro static builds: #1177 → #1178 → #1179 → #1180 → #1182 → #1183 → #1184 → #1185 → #1186 → #1187 → #1188 → #1189. With `ui: 'svelte'`, every page of the Astro 5 demo linked a 72 KB dialog stylesheet on top of the injected full stylesheet, which already has those rules. The dialog islands import `@c15t/ui` class maps. In the browser those modules also import their component CSS, and Astro links every stylesheet a page script can reach on every page. When the integration injects the full stylesheet, a new Vite plugin resolves browser-side `@c15t/ui/styles/components/` imports to the `.node.js` variant, which has the same class names and no CSS import. The server build already uses that variant through the `node` condition. With `styles: false` the plugin is not added, so the islands keep their own CSS. ## Astro bug: lazy chunk CSS deleted Since Astro 5.16.12, CSS imported by modules that are reachable only from an `injectScript('page', ...)` script is deleted from the build, whether the import is static or dynamic. The cause is the orphan check in `astro:rollup-plugin-inline-stylesheets` ([withastro/astro#14607](https://github.com/withastro/astro/pull/14607)): it looks for the sheet in a chunk's `importedAssets` but not in `importedCss`, where Vite records it. The same thing happens on Astro 7.3.5. This PR does not change that. With `styles` on, the injected stylesheets cover every rule. On the published alpha, which relies on the islands' own CSS, the IAB dialog surface loses about 120 of its classes. #1180 and this PR close that gap by injecting `@c15t/astro/iab/styles.css` whenever `iab` is set, and by leaving IAB class maps alone otherwise. ## Testing - Unit tests for the resolver: it points browser class maps at the no-CSS variant, and leaves the server build, `.css` subpaths and class maps without a variant alone. Another test checks the plugin is added only when `styles` is on. - `astro-demo` (Svelte, Astro 5) now emits one stylesheet, and pages no longer link `panel-surface.css`. - Both Astro example targets pass all journeys. > [!NOTE] > ### Fix duplicate stylesheet in Astro dialog islands via `c15t:class-maps-without-css` plugin > - Adds a Vite plugin `c15t:class-maps-without-css` in [class-map-plugin.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1188/files#diff-3c904e381e1432696ff3fa49add7fc3091cd774879c6865c4bc0358e0bd4e5db) that redirects browser class-map imports to their `.node.js` variant, avoiding the CSS-bearing module when the full stylesheet is already injected. > - The plugin skips SSR/server resolution, direct `.css` imports, missing variants, and IAB class maps unless the IAB stylesheet is also injected. > - [integration.ts](https://github.com/c15t/c15t/pull/1188/files#diff-b33047facc2c2c36ae72893d968e153c5658f06e67f34d8b339cf191ac064931) registers the plugin in `buildVitePlugins` when styles are enabled; it is omitted when `styles: false`. > - Behavioral Change: eligible browser imports of `@c15t/ui/styles/components/` now resolve to the `.node.js` variant instead of the CSS-bearing module; check `createClassMapPlugin` matchers if other components rely on the original resolution. > > > > Macroscope summarized b7a4098. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance** * Astro integrations with styles enabled now avoid loading unnecessary dialog CSS, reducing the amount of CSS sent to the browser. * Disabling styles continues to preserve the islands’ CSS. * **Compatibility** * The Astro integration now selects the appropriate client-side class-map variant while leaving server-side imports unchanged.

This fixes the definitions, adds a production consumer built from packed artifacts, and marks the superseded parts of the July gate report. No SDK package changes. ## What was wrong - **`repeat-visitor` measured first-time visitors in five of six harnesses.** React, Next.js and TanStack Start opened a new browser context without the stored choice. SvelteKit and Astro seeded a cookie stamped `i.t:1800000000000` (January 2027), which the cookie reader rejects as a future consent time. Only Nuxt measured a returning visitor. - **`bannerInFirstHtml` read the finished document.** It could not tell the first streamed chunk from a banner that arrives after an awaited consent resolution. - **Banner milestones were blurred.** `bannerPaintMs` fell back to a different reading, arms without a banner reported `bannerReadyMs = 0`, and nothing recorded FCP or LCP. - **Cold labels didn't say which caches were cold.** The Nuxt `--cold-manifest` token was only read at build time, so it never changed the URL of an existing build. ## Changes - `saved-consent-accept` and `saved-consent-reject` replace the fresh-context `repeat-visitor` arms (React, Next.js, TanStack Start). A fresh visit clicks accept or reject and its `storageState()` seeds a new context. Every sample fails the run if the banner shows in the DOM or server HTML, or if no stored choice is restored. Fresh visits must show the banner. SvelteKit and Astro use `createRepeatVisitorCookie()` and the same assertion. - `bannerInFirstChunk` and `bannerInServerHtml` come from a raw `accept-encoding: identity` HTTP read with the visit's cookies, plus arrival times for the first chunk and the banner markup. - The shared observer records `bannerDomMs`, `bannerFirstFrameMs`, Element Timing `bannerPaintMs`, `fcpMs` and `lcpMs`. `bannerReadyMs` stays the hydrated reading. Visits without a banner report `null`. - Every result carries `cacheBrowser`, `cacheSdkManifest`, `cacheFrameworkProcess`, `cacheCdnEdge: not-measured` and a `cacheSetup` sentence. - `bench:production-consumer` (in `nextjs-browser-bench`) packs c15t with `bun pm pack`, installs the tarballs into a Next.js 16 app outside the workspace, and runs interleaved arms. The app uses the aggregate stylesheet, a custom theme, `resolveConsent` under a Suspense boundary, and the deferred dialog. It reports stylesheet count, bytes and cross-stylesheet class overlap per route, and separates fresh, warm-browser-cache, cold-SDK-manifest and cold-process visits. - `benchmarks/reports/visit-definitions-2026-09-25/README.md` has the details. `gate-2026-07-05.md` now says which rows and gate claims are superseded, including the placeholder-driven hosted-client banner win from Addendum D. - Ports are configurable (`--port` / `C15T_BENCH_PORT`) in every harness. - **The React `C15T_CSS=styles` arm hasn't built since `bbfcc04bb`.** Its shim and extras imported `*.module.css` specifiers that now resolve to JavaScript class maps. Turbopack failed with `missing VAR_MODULE_GLOBAL_ERROR in template` and webpack with `Selector ":root" is not pure`. The shim also dropped `rights`, `rightLink` and the overlay classes the banner reads. The shim and aliases are gone because v3 class maps already are CSS-module maps. The default build imports `@c15t/react/styles.css`. The `C15T_CSS=styles` build imports the banner's five component stylesheets explicitly and builds into `.next-css-styles`. Component stylesheets carry no default tokens, so `banner-css` passes the full default theme in both builds. Without it, the component-CSS banner renders with a transparent card and square corners. Each `banner-css` sample now fails if the banner card is unstyled. ## Before / After Old harness (`v3` at `40032552c`) against this branch, same c15t build, same machine. docs(benchmarks): decompose the cold-start cost of a new Next process (#1196) The alpha.2 docs-site run showed a new `next start` process at 629 ms TTFB against 3 ms for a second request, with 7/7 origin `/manifest` calls. This PR adds a report and a runnable harness that measure the cache states separately. It changes no package code. Report: `benchmarks/reports/cold-start-decomposition-2026-09-25/README.md` ## Findings - **Why the site called the origin on every restart, and #1190's consumer did not:** the site passes `manifestRevalidateSeconds: 0` to `createNextConsentRouteHandlers`, which turns off the Next Data Cache and leaves only the SDK's in-process cache. That cache is empty in a new process. The handler default (300 s) writes the manifest to `.next/cache/fetch-cache`, which survives a restart. The consumer reproduces both: 9/9 origin calls on restart with the site's setting, 0/9 with the default. - **The 626 ms TTFB gap:** the manifest fetch contributes nothing. On the site build, the origin request leaves 110 ms (97–133) after the response headers; the brief's own samples show 106–212 ms. Loading c15t's share of the server chunks takes 3.3–4.2 ms before the first byte (and 2.4–2.8 ms after it), and no c15t code runs before the first byte. The rest comes from Next.js loading the site's route entries and modules on the first request. - **In a small app,** c15t adds about 25 ms to a cold first byte: about 14 ms for its modules in the page graph and about 11 ms for the first loopback to the manifest route. - **Manifest cache:** - 5 concurrent cold requests make 1 origin call, in a warm process and in a new one. - Stale-while-revalidate and the 5 s retry floor behave as documented. - With a cold failure (503) or a hang, the tracker stays blocked and the browser shows no banner. - **Not changed, for an owner to decide:** - A hanging backend on a cold cache holds page content for the route's 10 s fetch timeout. - A cold failure is not remembered, so each later request retries the origin. - Pointing `resolveConsent`'s `manifestURL` at the backend (off the documented path) bypasses both caches. - **Not measured:** the CDN edge, and Vercel's shared Data Cache. The seven-day CDN TTL was not tested. ## Before / After No fix, so "before" is the brief's combined measurement and "after" is the same cost split by state. Before, the brief: docs site, homepage, condition B, n = 7 pairs. | State | TTFB | FCP | Banner ready | Origin `/manifest` | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | New Next process | 629 ms | 1,392 ms | 2,025 ms | 7/7 | | Second request | 3 ms | 1,100 ms | 1,556 ms | 0/7 | After, packed-artifact consumer, condition L (+200 ms backend, no browser throttling). Medians with ranges; n = 9 per row; interleaved; load average 5.9–11.3. Condition B tables are in the report. | Config | State | TTFB | Banner in HTML | Banner ready | Origin `/manifest` | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Site-like (S) | a: warm process, warm manifest | 3 (2–6) | 8 (6–11) | 339 (54–347) | 0/9 | | Site-like (S) | b: warm process, cold manifest | 3 (3–4) | 209 (207–210) | 341 (338–358) | 9/9 | | Site-like (S) | c: new process, `.next/cache` kept | 89 (76–261) | 323 (305–582) | 426 (414–631) | 9/9 | | Site-like (S) | d: new process, `.next/cache` deleted | 82 (74–154) | 314 (306–412) | 424 (412–509) | 9/9 | | Site-like (S) | e: as d, instant backend | 83 (76–217) | 113 (111–263) | 326 (164–450) | 9/9 | | Default (D) | c: new process, `.next/cache` kept | 82 (74–134) | 117 (105–179) | 171 (155–239) | 0/9 | Site build, raw HTTP, new process per sample, `.next-860/cache` kept, +200 ms backend, n = 7, load average 6–7: | Part of the cold TTFB gap | Measured | | --- | ---: | | Cold first byte / warm first byte | 570 (515–651) / 4 (3–4) ms | | Manifest fetch inside TTFB | 0 ms (origin request sent 110 ms after the headers) | | c15t server chunk loading before the first byte | 3.3–4.2 ms (3 CPU profiles) | | c15t code run before the first byte | 0.0 ms (3 CPU profiles) | SHAs: base `origin/v3` `40032552c`. The consumer installs packages packed from `7eadda5b1` (#1191). Next.js 16.3.4, Node 24.19.0, Chromium 148. ## Reproduce ```sh bun turbo run build --filter=c15t... cd benchmarks/reports/cold-start-decomposition-2026-09-25/harness ./prepare.sh ../../../.. node mock-backend.mjs 4790 & node run.mjs --rounds 9 && node summarize.mjs node coldraw.mjs --reps 9 node cache.mjs ``` ## Checks - `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` pass on the new directory. - I rebuilt the harness from the committed files into a fresh work dir and ran every script. It reproduces the same pattern. - No package code changed, so there are no package tests, type checks, or release note. ## Review fixes - `analyze-profile.mjs` now applies the TTFB cutoff to file loads; rerunning it on the site profiles changed c15t chunk loading before the first byte from 3.4–4.4 ms to 3.3–4.2 ms. fix(ui): load each component stylesheet rule once (#1191) The `@c15t/ui/styles/components/` class maps imported their own stylesheet, and `styles.css` carries the same rules. A Next.js 16 Turbopack production build of the documented setup (`@import 'c15t/react/styles.css'` plus prebuilt components) therefore shipped the same component rules twice, as separate CSS assets. This PR removes the CSS import from the class maps, so each rule loads once. ## CSS-loading contract - **React, Next.js, TanStack Start, Svelte, Astro:** the app imports `styles.css` (or `styles.tw3.css`) once. It holds every component rule, the default tokens and the shared primitive styles. Components load no CSS of their own. A component rendered without the stylesheet is unstyled. That was already true in practice: removing the aggregate on alpha.2 left the dialog broken because tokens and primitive rules only live in the aggregate. - **Vue / Nuxt:** components include their styles, as the Vue quickstart says. Vue components now import `@c15t/ui/styles/components/.css` next to each class map instead of relying on the class map to do it. Vue apps emit the same CSS files as before, byte for byte. Default tokens come from the Vue plugin config at runtime, as before. - **Per-component `.css` exports** stay published for hosts that assemble their own stylesheet. They hold one component's rules and no tokens or primitive rules. - **Class maps** (`.js` and `.node.js`) are now identical and CSS-free under every export condition. The `node` condition and `*.node.js` subpaths stay for compatibility. ## Cause `packages/ui/scripts/generate-style-artifacts.ts` kept `import "./.css"` in `.js`, which the `import` condition serves to bundlers. `packages/react` (and Svelte, Astro) import those class maps, for example `components/prompt/prompt.js` → `@c15t/ui/styles/components/consent-banner` → `prompt.js` → `prompt.css`. Next's client graph turned each of those side-effect imports into its own stylesheet, next to the global one that already inlines `styles.css`: | Extra asset (alpha.2) | Contents | Pulled in by | | --- | --- | --- | | `0r84qk585kd6s.css`, 18,278 B | `prompt.css` | `ConsentBanner` | | `26wn2-vv6-4op.css`, 25,916 B | `consent-actions.css`, `branding.css`, `button.css` | banner actions | | `10m2etv5psngl.css`, 1,459 B | `legal-links.css` | banner legal links | | `3bphc3-q_ba9v.css`, 2,093 B | `frame.css` | `ConsentGate` re-export | | 3 more on dialog open | `panel.css`, `panel-trigger.css`, accordion/switch/preference-item/vendor-list | deferred dialog | Three of these have the same content hashes as the extra stylesheets on the c15t docs site. Primitive class maps already had their CSS import stripped for the same reason, and 2.x stripped both. The duplicates also change the cascade. If a layout imports a consent component before its global CSS, the component stylesheets load first and declare `@layer components` before Tailwind 4 declares `theme, base, components, utilities`. Tailwind's preflight then outranks c15t, and the banner buttons lose their background and radius. See the second screenshot table. ## Before / After Minimal Next.js 16.3.4 App Router consumer, Turbopack production build, installed from packed tarballs (not workspace links). It mirrors the docs site: Tailwind 4 + `@import 'c15t/react/styles.css'`, the site's colour-only custom theme (light/dark via `next-themes`), a page-wide `Suspense` around `await resolveConsent()` from `c15t/next/server` resolving a captured manifest, `ConsentBanner` rendered on the server, the deferred `ConsentDialog`, and a `ConsentGate` re-export. Before: `origin/v3` `40032552c` (alpha.2). After: this branch `7eadda5b1`. Chromium 1223 (Playwright), 1280×720. ### Emitted CSS (both `/` and `/docs`) | | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Stylesheets on first load | 5 | 1 | | First-load CSS, raw / gzip | 184,028 B / 24,948 B | 136,282 B / 18,122 B | | Stylesheets after opening the dialog | 8 | 1 | | CSS after opening the dialog, raw / gzip | 231,029 B / 32,949 B | 136,282 B / 18,122 B | | CSS rules present in more than one asset | 399 | 0 | | CSS transfer on first load (resource timing) | 26,729 B | 18,649 B | The global stylesheet is byte-identical in both builds (same hash). ### First contentful paint Interleaved ABAB, one warm-up per arm and route, fresh browser context and disabled cache per sample. Medians, range in brackets. | Conditions | Route | n per arm | Before | After | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | CDP 4× CPU, 170 ms, 1,125,000 B/s down, 187,500 B/s up, **HTTP/2** (local TLS proxy) | `/` | 11 | 504 ms (500–508) | 496 ms (488–500) | | same | `/docs` | 11 | 520 ms (512–548) | 504 ms (492–524) | | same profile, **HTTP/1.1** direct to `next start` | `/` | 11 | 436 ms (432–444) | 468 ms (464–476) | | same | `/docs` | 11 | 444 ms (440–456) | 480 ms (472–492) | | Lighthouse 13.5.0 mobile, simulated throttling | `/` | 7 | 1,204 ms (1,054–1,206) | 904 ms (903–905) | | same | `/docs` | 7 | 1,203 ms (1,053–1,212) | 904 ms (903–905) | The HTTP/1.1 row got slower, and the stylesheet itself did not cause it. Request timing shows why: with alpha.2, the four extra render-blocking stylesheets hold five of Chrome's six HTTP/1.1 connections, so the low-priority async scripts wait, and the global stylesheet gets the throttled pipe mostly to itself (done at 402 ms). With one stylesheet, the scripts download alongside it and CDP throttling splits bandwidth evenly regardless of priority, so the same 18,740-byte file finishes at 430 ms. Over HTTP/2, which is what a CDN serves, the fix is 8–16 ms faster. Lighthouse's model, which charges a round trip per render-blocking request, shows about 300 ms. Machine load averages (1 min) during runs: HTTP/2 11.4 → 9.8, HTTP/1.1 6.9 → 8.5, Lighthouse 9.9 → 10.4. fix(react): load the consent dialog before its first open (#1193) ## Summary The deferred `` downloads its chunk (10 KB gzip) on first use. Before this PR, only `ConsentBanner.PolicyActions` started that download early, so the stock banner and every other dialog opener waited for the chunk after the click. This PR makes the dialog load before the first open in three ways: - **Hover and focus.** `ConsentButton` warms the dialog on focus and pointer enter when `action="open-consent-dialog"`. That covers the stock banner's Customize button, `PolicyActions`, `ConsentDialogLink`, the `ConsentGate` button and the widget's Customize button. `ConsentDialogTrigger` does the same. Handlers passed as `onFocus` or `onPointerEnter` still run. - **Idle time.** A tap, or focus and Enter together, leaves no lead time for hover or focus. While the banner is shown or a dialog opener is mounted, the dialog now loads in the first idle period after the page's `load` event (`requestIdleCallback`, or 200 ms after `load` in Safari). It's skipped with Save-Data, on `2g`/`slow-2g` and offline, where hover and focus still load it. `preloadDialog: 'intent'` in the provider options (or `ConsentRoot`'s `options`) turns idle loading off. A saved-consent visit with nothing on the page that opens the dialog downloads nothing extra. - **Failed preloads retry.** A preload that failed used to be cached, so the later open threw the same error. With the first commit's focus warming, a failed chunk request on focus left the dialog unopenable until reload. Only a rendered export caches a failure now, so after a failed preload the next hover, focus or open retries the import. The dialog still isn't part of first-load JS. ### Eval at idle, or download only? I measured both. The network-only arm preloads the same chunk at idle with `` and evaluates it on open. - Evaluating at idle costs 2.6 ms of `EvaluateScript` at 4× CPU (3.2 ms of task time in all, longest task 2.8 ms), well below the 50 ms long-task threshold. - Deferring the evaluation to the open saves nothing measurable: focus and Enter 3 s after load takes 38.4 ms evaluated at idle and 39.1 ms network-only (B, 4×). - A library can't portably learn a bundler's chunk URL without importing the chunk. So the idle path calls `import()`. ## Before / After Next.js 16.3.4 production consumer from the combined v2/v3 run, built from packed tarballs: Tailwind 4, colour-only theme, page-wide ``, promise layout, footer `ConsentDialogLink`, `/docs` page. perf(nextjs): send the first manifest-mode save without loading the resolver (#1194) With `ConsentRoot` and a `manifestURL` config (the documented App Router setup), the first Accept, Reject or Save downloaded the manifest resolver chunk before `POST /subjects` went out. That chunk is 63,877 B gzip, mostly all-locale translations. When the server has already resolved the visitor's state, the browser never runs init, so nothing in that chunk is needed to save. This PR makes `ConsentRoot`'s lazy manifest transport send saves, identity links, subject reads and privacy directives through the hosted transport until init starts loading the resolver. Both transports send the same request to the same route. Once a browser init loads the resolver, every call goes through it as before. ## Why the backend check is unaffected The backend recomputes the decision from `policyId`, `fingerprint`, `country`, `region`, `language` and `gpc` on `POST /subjects` and rejects a mismatch with `STALE_POLICY`. The kernel puts those values on every save payload from the server-resolved snapshot (`saveDecisionInputs`), and `buildDecisionAssertion` prefers them over anything the transport remembered. The manifest transport only has its own remembered inputs after a browser init, which this path never runs. Checked in a production consumer: the POST path, header names and body (subject id and timestamps masked) are identical between alpha.2, this branch, and `hosted()`. One visible difference: if the save fails, the `onError` message says `c15t hosted transport` instead of `c15t manifest transport`. ## Before / After Production Next.js 16.3.4 consumer installed from packed tarballs (issue 3's App Router guide arm: `ConsentRoot`, `manifestURL`, SSR `resolveConsent` inside ``, custom theme, animations on). Before is alpha.2 (`40032552c`), after is this branch (`08659da9c`), `hosted()` is the site-shaped arm for reference. 7 measured samples plus 1 warm-up per cell, arms interleaved with rotating order. A: native CPU, no throttling. B: 4× CPU, 170 ms latency, 1,125,000 B/s down, 187,500 B/s up. Busy: a 40 ms long task every 160 ms. Load average 8.2 at start, 6.7 at end (other benchmarks were running on the machine). This PR deletes the old lazy manifest block, and #1192 adds `lazyOffline` directly below it. To resolve it, delete the old block and keep `lazyOffline`. The banner disappears on the same frame in both versions, and Event Timing's click duration is 24 ms in every arm. - The site's 3–8 ms "v3 slower from click to recorded" did not reproduce in this consumer. - Selector hooks do reduce renders. perf(core,nextjs): load the hosted init path only when init runs (#1206) > **Stack:** layer 7 of 36 in stack #1225 on `v3`, based on #1194, so its diff now shows only this PR's commits. ## What was loading A Next.js App Router page with `ConsentRoot` resolves the visitor's state on the server, so the browser never runs init. Its first load still carried the hosted transport's init path, because the record requests (save, identify, subject read, privacy directive) and init lived in one object: - `createHostedTransport` itself (init request, header allowlist, prefetch hand-off), `libs/request-context`, `libs/prefetch/prefetch` (including the server-side `buildPrefetchScript` string) and `@c15t/schema`'s `geo-headers`. - `transports/subject-record`, which only runs when a subject record is read back after a user switch. - `transports/mode.js`, pulled in by `custom()`: it shared a module with `hosted()`, and bundlers keep or drop whole modules, so any app calling `custom()` shipped the hosted transport. V8 coverage on the packed consumer showed `request-context` at 4%, `prefetch` at 9% and `subject-record` at 5% executed across a plain load, a saved-consent visit, Accept and opening the dialog (module-level statements only). ## Change - `@c15t/core` adds `createHostedRecordTransport()`: save, identify, `loadSubjectRecord` and `recordPrivacyOptOut`, with the same routes, bodies and decision assertion as before. `createHostedTransport()` is now that record half plus `init`, and loads the subject-record reviver on the first `loadSubjectRecord()` call. - `custom()` moves to `transports/custom.ts`; `mode.ts` re-exports it. - `@c15t/nextjs` generalizes #1194's lazy manifest transport into `createLazyInitTransport(records, load)`. `ConsentRoot`'s hosted modes (`backendURL` only, and `initURL`) use `lazyHosted()`: records go out through the record transport at once, and `hosted-mode.ts` (the full transport) loads on the first init. Once init has started, every request goes through the loaded transport, as in manifest mode. With `assertDecisionInputs`, a save that carries no decision inputs is still refused before init, as the full transport does. Both halves use the `fetch` that was global when the transport was created, as before. - When the browser runs init (a static export with `state={{}}`, cookie-only `resolveConsent()`, or a failed server init), `lazyHosted()` sends the first `/init` at the same time as the `hosted-mode` chunk request, and the loaded transport picks up that response. It reuses it only when the URL, method, credentials and headers match exactly. Both halves build the request with a new core helper, `createHostedInitRequest()`, which `createHostedTransport` also uses. When an inline prefetch script exists and there is no `initURL`, nothing is sent early, so the loaded transport still reads the prefetch. No chunk sits between Accept and the POST or the cookie write: the save path has no dynamic import. **Builds on #1194.** The Next.js side extends `lazy-manifest-transport.ts`, which #1194 adds, so this branch contains #1194's commit until it merges. `root.tsx` conflicts with #1192 the same way #1194 does; the integration branch resolves it by keeping #1192's `lazyOffline()` and importing only `custom` from `@c15t/react`. ## Regression tests - `packages/core/src/__tests__/hosted-record-graph.test.ts` walks the static import graph: the record transport must not reach `hosted.ts`, `init-output`, `subject-record`, `request-context`, `prefetch` or `extractConsentRequestInputs`; `hosted.ts` must not statically reach `subject-record`; `custom.ts` must not reach `hosted.ts`. It also covers the record transport's save body, the refused save and the subject read. Restoring a static `subject-record` import fails two of the graph tests. - `packages/nextjs/src/__tests__/lazy-manifest-transport.test.ts` adds `lazyHosted` tests (save posts without loading, refusal under `assertDecisionInputs`, one load for several inits, `fetch` captured at creation) and scans `root.tsx` and `lazy-manifest-transport.ts` for static imports of `hosted`, `createHostedTransport`, `./hosted-mode` or the manifest resolver. Restoring `import { custom, hosted } from '@c15t/react'` fails it. - The same file checks that `/init` goes out while the `hosted-mode` chunk is still loading (it fails on this PR's first version), that the loaded transport reuses the early response, and that it leaves an inline prefetch alone. `packages/core/src/__tests__/hosted-record-graph.test.ts` checks that the new request-builder modules don't reach the init path. ## Before / After Next.js 16.3.4 App Router consumer (Turbopack, `cacheComponents`, streamed `resolveConsent` layout from #1195, the site's colour theme) built from packed tarballs outside the workspace. Merge the PRs below it first. ## What was loading `ConsentProvider` mounts `IframeBlockerMount` unless `iframeBlocker: false`. It called `useIframeBlocker`, which imports `@c15t/core/modules/iframe-blocker` in a mount effect. So every page downloaded and ran the blocker right after hydration, iframes or not. The watcher moves `src` to `data-src` and sets `data-c15t-paused`, the same state the blocker leaves a denied frame in, so the blocker restores it once consent allows it. A frame the snapshot allows (checked with core's `evaluateConsent`, which is already in the first-load bundle) is left alone. - `iframeBlocker: { disableAutomaticBlocking: true }` and the public `useIframeBlocker()` hook still load the blocker at mount.
